def factor_range_asymmetry_longer(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    df_copy['range'] = df_copy['high'] - df_copy['low']
    df_copy['up'] = (df_copy['close'] > df_copy['close'].shift(1)).astype(float)
    df_copy['down'] = (df_copy['close'] < df_copy['close'].shift(1)).astype(float)
    up_range_sum = (df_copy['range'] * df_copy['up']).rolling(60).sum()
    up_count = df_copy['up'].rolling(60).sum().replace(0, np.nan)
    down_range_sum = (df_copy['range'] * df_copy['down']).rolling(60).sum()
    down_count = df_copy['down'].rolling(60).sum().replace(0, np.nan)
    up_mean = up_range_sum / up_count
    down_mean = down_range_sum / down_count
    factor = down_mean / up_mean
    factor.name = 'factor_range_asymmetry_longer'
    return factor
formula: ratio = rolling_mean(high-low | down) / rolling_mean(high-low | up) over 60 days
rationale: Captures asymmetric volatility by comparing average intraday range on downtrend days versus uptrend days. Using a longer 60-day window produces a more stable estimate of the leverage effect, reducing noise while preserving the core economic mechanism.
